If you can, post your data and give us something more to go on. If you can't post your real data, make up some fake data that is similar or recode it. 

You should look at D. Kahle's ggmap package as a starter. 

I suspect you will need to use facet_grid() to get your 2x2 maps for comparison across two factors. 

We can get no further without data. 

HTH,

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: drawing maps with ggplot2 in R
parts:
Mokoena, 

I plotted the data you gave me and it just looks like a grid of dots centered over Lesotho. I hope this is what you intended. 



library(readr)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr) #library(magrittr) really just need the pipe
library(ggplot2)
library(ggmap)


mapdata <- read_csv("~/Downloads/test.csv") %>%
gather(Year, Value, -lon, -lat) #gather up years

map <- get_map(location= c(lon=mean(mapdata$lon), lat = mean(mapdata$lat)), zoom = 6, maptype = "toner", source = "stamen")

ggmap(map) + 
  geom_point(data = mapdata, aes(x=lon, y=lat), color = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~Year, ncol=2)
